subject: Post-demo: SLO checklist & next steps
message_1_body:
Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time to demo this morning. Quick recap focused on the performance/SLO items you asked us to confirm so your engineering team can evaluate fit. I captured the items we discussed and next steps below.

SLO checklist (as discussed on the call):
- Latency targets: p95 <200ms (text-gen endpoints, 2048 context), p99 <400ms.
- Throughput: sustained 200 reqs/s per model instance, with burst capacity to 1,000 reqs/s across the fleet.
- Concurrency: baseline concurrency target 50 concurrent sessions; support for spikes to 400 concurrent sessions during peak business hours.
- Streaming: partial-token streaming supported; chunk latency goal <50ms from model to client for the first token in a chunk.
- Token payloads: average 120 input tokens / 60 response tokens for your anticipated flows (please confirm if average differs).

Attachments: I attached the SLO-checklist PDF we ran through in the demo.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Confirm average tokens per request and typical concurrency distribution (p95, median, peak).
2) Redwood will provision a short-lived POC environment (dedicated pool) for load testing.
3) Run a focused load test (we can help run or run together) to validate p95/p99 and streaming chunk latencies.
4) Align on decision criteria (latency targets, cost per 1M tokens, failover behavior).

Can you confirm the items above and share the team’s preferred day/time for a 30–45m scoping call next week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Schedule: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/30
Redwood Inference
message_2_subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO checklist & next steps
message_2_body:
Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency: p95 <200ms looks reasonable as a target. For p99, we need visibility into the distribution under burst. Can you include historical p99 numbers from your hosted profiles or similar benchmarks for devices with 32GB A40 / A100-class GPUs?

2) Concurrency vs throughput: our traffic is bursty — baseline concurrency will be ~40, but we can see bursts up to ~400 concurrent users during promo spikes, which translates to short peaks of ~900–1,200 reqs/s sustained for 1–2 minutes. We need a plan for graceful degradation (model fallback or queueing behavior) when capacity is constrained.

3) Streaming: critical for our product. The chunk-first-token latency <50ms target is tight. Can you describe how Redwood measures chunk latency and whether the POC can include an RTT-limited test (we can run from our EC2 region)?

4) Tokens: our initial estimator of avg tokens is close to what you listed (120/60), but we have flows up to 600 tokens in some sessions. Should we model that in the POC?

I'm happy to take the scoping call. My team is available Tues/Wed next week 10–12 PT.

message_3_subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO checklist & next steps
message_3_body:
Samir —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the details — very helpful. Short answers inline and a suggested Mutual Action Plan (MAP):

Latency/p99 references:
- We will share anonymized benchmark p99/p95 for models running on 80GB A100 and 40GB A40 profiles. Historically, p99 for 2048 context on similar models is ~250–350ms in our hosted runs; p95 is typically <180ms. We'll include the model variant and kernel profile in the POC notes.

Concurrency/throughput fallbacks:
- Redwood supports automated routing policies: during sustained high bursts we can route to a higher-capacity variant (larger batch/quantized model) or apply queueing with a max-wait SLA. We recommend a canary plan: start with a dedicated pool sized for 200 sustained / 400 burst capacity, run load test, then scale to production reserved pool if metrics meet decision criteria.

Streaming test approach:
- For chunk latency, we measure time from model emit to the edge egress; POC will include an RTT-controlled test run from your EC2 region to isolate network latency. We'll instrument per-chunk latency (first-byte and subsequent chunk times) in our test harness.

Token payloads:
- Please include 600-token flows in one of the POC scenarios so we can validate tail behavior.

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — timeline (2–3 weeks):
1) This week: confirm exact token distributions + provide a sample traffic profile (JSON or csv).
2) Week 1: Redwood provisions dedicated POC pool and share load-test script + instructions.
3) Week 1–2: Joint load test (we can run together during an agreed window). Redwood will produce a POC report with p50/p95/p99 and streaming chunk latencies.
4) Week 2–3: Review results and align on sizing for Dedicated (reserved) pool + pricing sketch.
5) Decision: go/no-go based on p99 <400ms for 600-token flows and acceptable cost profile.

Attachments: MAP spreadsheet attached (with proposed timelines & owners). Also linking the HubSpot deal page and the load-test sandbox we will provision.

Proposed times for scoping call: Tue 10:30–11:15 PT or Wed 10:00–10:45 PT — feel free to pick via my calendar link.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP-Redwood-FintechCo.xlsx
